qs.q: A patient with schizophrenia is prescribed a typical antipsychotic. They develop tremors and rigidity. Which mechanism best explains this side effect?
o: The drug inhibits the reuptake of norepinephrine causing vasoconstriction
The drug enhances serotonin 5-HT2A receptors leading to muscle tone
The drug blocks dopamine D2 receptors in the nigrostriatal pathway
The drug increases the activity of GABA in basal ganglia to reduce
The drug blocks histamine H1 receptors causing sedation and relaxation
qs.e: Typical antipsychotics block D2 receptors in the nigrostriatal pathway, leading to extrapyramidal side effects.

qs.q: A patient with schizophrenia is prescribed an atypical antipsychotic. They report feeling less anxious but still have auditory hallucinations. Which mechanism best explains the residual hallucinations?
o: The medication blocks GABA activity, increasing neuronal excitability.
The medication boosts serotonin activity, potentially worsening hallucinations.
The medication inhibits dopamine reuptake, raising dopamine levels.
The medication has lower D2 affinity, leading to incomplete dopamine blockade.
The medication increases acetylcholine activity, causing cognitive impairment.
qs.e: Atypical antipsychotics have lower D2 affinity, which may lead to incomplete blockade of positive symptoms.
